subject: Polity
description: Articles 12-35: 6 categories of FRs, scope, restrictions, key cases

questions.stem: FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS in the Indian Constitution are guaranteed under which Part?
questions.explanation: Part III of the Constitution = Fundamental Rights, Articles 12-35. Originally 7 categories; right to property removed by 44th Amendment (1978) → now 6 categories: (1) RIGHT TO EQUALITY (14-18); (2) RIGHT TO FREEDOM (19-22); (3) RIGHT AGAINST EXPLOITATION (23-24); (4) FREEDOM OF RELIGION (25-28); (5) CULTURAL + EDUCATIONAL RIGHTS (29-30); (6) RIGHT TO CONSTITUTIONAL REMEDIES (32) — Ambedkar called this 'heart and soul'.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Right to LIFE + Personal Liberty is enshrined in which Article?
questions.explanation: Article 21 — 'No person shall be deprived of his LIFE or PERSONAL LIBERTY except according to procedure established by law.' Most expanded right: Maneka Gandhi (1978) — procedure must be just, fair, reasonable, not arbitrary; Sunil Batra; Olga Tellis (right to livelihood); Vishaka (sexual harassment guidelines); Right to PRIVACY (Puttaswamy 2017, 9-judge bench); Right to die with dignity (passive euthanasia, 2018); right to clean environment, food, shelter, health, education (Mohini Jain, Unni Krishnan), speedy trial, legal aid — all read into Article 21. India's most powerful right.

questions.stem: Article 19(1) gives 6 freedoms. Which one was REMOVED by the 44th Amendment in 1978?

options.option_text: Freedom of speech and expression remained
Freedom to acquire and hold private property
Freedom of profession, trade and occupation
Freedom to assemble peacefully without arms

questions.explanation: Article 19(1) originally had 7 freedoms: (a) speech + expression; (b) assembly peaceably without arms; (c) form associations; (d) move freely throughout India; (e) reside + settle anywhere in India; (f) ACQUIRE, HOLD, DISPOSE OF PROPERTY — DELETED by 44th Amendment (1978); (g) practise any profession / carry on trade. Right to property was made a LEGAL right (Article 300A) instead of fundamental — to enable land reforms + nationalisation without constitutional challenges. So now 6 freedoms in 19(1).

questions.stem: Article 14 ensures EQUALITY before LAW. It applies to:
questions.explanation: Article 14: 'The State shall not deny to any PERSON equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.' Note 'PERSON' (not 'citizen') — applies to ALL HUMAN BEINGS in India, including foreigners. Even legal persons (companies). Other rights for citizens-only: Articles 15, 16, 19, 29. Rights for all: 14, 20, 21, 21A, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28. Concept of equality = (1) Equality BEFORE law (negative, British); (2) Equal PROTECTION of laws (positive, US-influenced).

questions.stem: Article 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies) allows a citizen to move directly to the:

options.option_text: High Court of the relevant state
Tribunal of Constitution as first step

questions.explanation: Article 32 — guarantees the right to MOVE THE SUPREME COURT directly for enforcement of Fundamental Rights. AMBEDKAR called Article 32 the 'HEART AND SOUL of the Constitution'. SC can issue 5 WRITS: HABEAS CORPUS (produce body — illegal detention); MANDAMUS (we command — order to a public official); PROHIBITION (don't act — to lower court); CERTIORARI (be informed — quash a lower court's order); QUO WARRANTO (by what authority — challenge official's right to public office). Article 226 — gives HIGH COURTS the same writ jurisdiction (broader: not limited to FRs). Article 32 itself is a FUNDAMENTAL RIGHT — cannot be removed except by constitutional amendment.

questions.stem: Right to Education (RTE) was added as a Fundamental Right by the 86th Amendment as Article:
questions.explanation: Article 21A — added by 86th Amendment (2002): 'The State shall provide FREE AND COMPULSORY EDUCATION to all children of the age of 6 to 14 years.' Operationalised by RTE ACT (2009), in force from 1 April 2010. Mandates: free seats up to ~25% in private schools for disadvantaged sections; minimum standards for schools; teacher-pupil ratios; no detention up to Class 8 (later relaxed). Same Amendment also: (a) made education 11th Fundamental Duty for parents (Article 51A(k)); (b) modified DPSP (Article 45 — early childhood education for under-6s).

questions.stem: Article 25 grants FREEDOM OF RELIGION. Which religious activity does it NOT directly protect?

options.option_text: Forced conversion of others by inducement

questions.explanation: Article 25(1) — freedom to PROFESS, PRACTISE + PROPAGATE religion (subject to public order, morality, health). 'Propagate' includes the right to spread one's faith, but does NOT include the right to CONVERT OTHERS by force, inducement, or fraud (Stanislaus case 1977). Many states have passed ANTI-CONVERSION laws (Odisha 1967, MP 1968, recently UP 2021, MP 2021, Karnataka 2022 etc.) — controversial. Other sub-clauses: 25(2) — state can regulate non-religious activities, social welfare reform (e.g., temple entry for all). Religious-freedom rights apply to all PERSONS (citizens + non-citizens).
